💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in a low-income year, like early retirement or a gap between jobs, you can sell investments held over a year free of federal tax while your taxable income, gains included, stays in the 0% bracket.
  • It has been revealed that this year the IRS puts the top of the 0% bracket for long-term gains, on investments held more than a year, at $98,900 of taxable income for a married couple filing jointly and $49,450 for a single filer.
  • Taxable income is income after deductions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in a low-income year, like early retirement or a gap between jobs, you can sell investments held over a year free of federal tax while your taxable income, gains included, stays in the 0% bracket. Sell up to the bracket’s top and buy back what you want to keep, so a later sale is taxed only on newer gains.

It has been revealed that this year the IRS puts the top of the 0% bracket for long-term gains, on investments held more than a year, at $98,900 of taxable income for a married couple filing jointly and $49,450 for a single filer. They rise to $102,100 and $51,050 in 2027.

Taxable income is income after deductions. Your room is the top minus the rest of the year’s taxable income, dividends included. Only the profit counts, not the whole sale price, and profit past the top is taxed at the next rate, 15%.

According to recent reports, A married couple who retire at 60 with $40,000 of taxable income can sell long-held funds at a $50,000 gain and owe no federal tax on it. On a Marketplace health plan, though, the gain counts as income for the premium tax credit that lowers their premiums. Since 2026, the IRS allows no credit when household income tops 400% of the poverty line, and any advance payments must be repaid.

The 0% rate is federal, so your state may still tax the gain. If you collect Social Security, the gain can make more of your benefits taxable, and each newly taxable dollar shrinks your room by a dollar.

The wash sale rule only blocks deducting a loss when you rebuy within 30 days. So you can buy the shares back the same day and still take the gain at 0%, unless your mutual fund limits quick buybacks. The rebuy resets your cost basis, the figure future gains are measured from, to today’s price. The new shares need more than a year to qualify for the long-term rate again.

Parents can pass this break to a grown child just starting out by giving appreciated shares, which keep your cost basis and the time you’ve held them.

According to recent reports, first settle what you’ll take from traditional IRAs or move into a Roth, since both are taxable income that fills the room before gains do. Then sell in December, once the year’s income is clear. The trade date decides which year’s return the gain goes on, so place the sale by the year’s last trading day.

According to recent reports, palmer was midspan on the Tunitas Creek Bridge, southbound, when the boat came into view through the gunsight notch of the arroyo. It was a Whaler circling clockwise fast and tight, maybe a quarter mile beyond the surf.

He’d wanted to ride a few waves at a sandbar that had been assembling itself over the past few days at Pomponio. A quick lunch-break session before the wind came up. But then he got the call about the boat, and now that he saw it spinning he also saw that his day was officially fucked. He crossed the bridge and powered up the Coast Highway to the overlook at the top of the rise. He lifted his Bushnells from the dashboard and got out of the truck and glassed the vessel.

The wake’s widening spiral told him the wheel had been hard to starboard a good long while. It looked to be stirring up some kind of suicidal whirlpool.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pay a store card’s balance in full by the first due date, and its checkout discount is yours to keep.
  • Say the clerk offers 15% off a $600 TV if you open the store’s card today.
  • That leaves you about $3 ahead of paying $600 up front.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pay a store card’s balance in full by the first due date, and its checkout discount is yours to keep. If you’d carry the purchase instead, a year of interest at the card’s rate, often above 30%, can cost as much as the discount saves. That’s still cheaper than carrying it on a typical credit card.

Say the clerk offers 15% off a $600 TV if you open the store’s card today. That’s $90 off. But pay off the remaining $510 in 12 equal monthly payments at a 30% annual percentage rate (APR), and by our math the interest comes to about $87.

That leaves you about $3 ahead of paying $600 up front. If you’d carry the TV either way, the store card is still cheaper than a general-purpose card, at the cost of a hard inquiry on your credit report. Those averaged a 25% APR in 2024, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) found. By our math, 12 payments on $600 at that rate cost about $84 in interest, so the store card comes out about $88 ahead. Store-only cards averaged 31%, and many charge every cardholder the same rate, so strong credit won’t get you a lower one.

In a recent development, FICO indicates a hard inquiry takes less than five points off most people’s scores and stops counting after a year. If your credit is strong, a store-only card’s starting limit is typically less than half what a general-purpose card would give you, the CFPB found. So the same $510 balance takes up a bigger share of the limit. That raises your credit utilization, which can lower your score until you pay it down.

After the first purchase, the card is worth using only if you shop there constantly and pay it in full every month. If you shop there only now and then, a no-annual-fee card that earns 2% back on everything you buy is the better everyday card. For the store’s rewards, ask whether it also offers a co-branded card, which many big retailers do. It carries the store’s name but works at other stores too.

Financing that’s interest-free only if you pay in full by a deadline is deferred interest, a different deal with risks of its own.

Take the discount only on something you came to buy, and pay the card off before you charge anything else to it.

The 101 money moves that matter most, from the foundations to protecting what you’ve built.

Getting Rich Is Easy Compared To Finding And Keeping Love

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2280 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Financialsamurai

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a parent, I have two main concerns for my children.
  • Will they be able to earn a livable wage in a world where AI keeps eating entry-level jobs?
  • Industry observers note that the second concern is bigger.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a parent, I have two main concerns for my children.

The first is economic stability. Will they be able to earn a livable wage in a world where AI keeps eating entry-level jobs? I question the time and money we spend educating our kids all the time. So I've been aggressively saving and investing for their future, just in case.

Industry observers note that the second concern is bigger. Will my children find love?

It has been revealed that A net worth target gets more achievable the more you save and the more time goes by. Compounding is boring, but it's reliable. If the direction is correct, sooner or later you will get there.

Industry observers note that finding a partner is far more amorphous. Our kids can work on their communication skills, fitness, charm, education, hygiene, empathy, and finances. But all of that merely improves their odds. There are no guarantees.

Which brings me to the strangest business story of 2026.

It has been revealed that in late October, The Fresh York Times reported that U.S. officials concluded a Chinese citizen named Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a Chinese intelligence asset. She is a senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center company and Nvidia cloud partner that rents computing power to Chinese firms.

Surveillance of her reportedly revealed a close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. And no, they are not related. Huang is a common surname like Smith.

Industry observers note that the Financial Times then reported that a U.S. government memo described the relationship as romantic. Her alleged goal was to gather information on Jensen and advanced AI chips, and to nudge him to lobby for looser chip exports to China.

The allegations come from anonymous officials and haven't been tested publicly. Officials reportedly don't believe Jensen knew about any intelligence activity. Nvidia claims his interactions with her were routine customer meetings. China denies the whole thing. House Republican committee chairs want a closed-door briefing on November 18.

So nobody outside the room knows the full story, except that Jensen admitted to the affair and is no longer CEO as of November 23, 2026. The lessons about love and money are worth discussing regardless of how the facts shake out.

According to recent reports, jensen Huang is worth over $120 billion (once $170 billion). He runs a manufacturer worth about $4 trillion after the sell-off. He is the closest thing we have to a modern-day emperor, the face of the AI revolution, mobbed like a rock star everywhere he goes in Taiwan.

And yet, if the reporting is accurate, it still wasn't enough.

There's a line from Gemma Teller Morrow in the TV show, Sons of Anarchy: “Only men need to be loved, sweetheart. Women need to be wanted.”.

Sources indicate that it's not entirely true. Everybody wants to be loved and desired to some degree. But the line points to something uncomfortable. No amount of money, applause, or leather jackets fills the need to feel admired by one specific person who seems to see you.

We all just want to be loved and accepted for who we are.

Here's the twist that makes this story sadder.

Sources indicate that if U.S. officials are right, what may have felt like admiration was tradecraft. Attentiveness, respect, and flattery are exactly what an intelligence service would deploy against the most vital man in AI. Intelligence services have used romance as an opening for as long as there have been secrets worth stealing.

Which exposes the hidden problem of extreme wealth and power. The richer you get, the harder it becomes to know whether anyone loves you for you. Every upcoming person in your life has a reason to be nice to you. Normal people get to skip that existential headache.

Money doesn't make finding love easier. Past a certain point, it makes find true love harder.

The people worth keeping are the ones who liked you before you were worth liking.

Jensen is far from the first emperor to create a commotion over love for a woman.

Industry observers note that paris and Helen of Troy. The Greeks' foundational story is about a prince who ran off with another man's wife and got his entire city burned to the ground. Myth, sure. But the Greeks clearly understood the risk.

According to recent reports, mark Antony and Cleopatra. Antony controlled half the Roman world. He chose Cleopatra over Rome, lost at Actium in 31 BC, and both were dead within a year. Octavian got the empire.

In a recent development, king Edward VIII. In 1936, he abdicated the British throne after less than a year to marry Wallis Simpson, a twice-divorced American. He traded a kingdom for love, and spent the rest of his life in comfortable, irrelevant exile.

John Profumo. The closest parallel to the Jensen story. In 1963, Britain's Secretary of State for War was revealed to have had an affair with Christine Keeler, who was also involved with a Soviet naval attaché. Profumo lied to Parliament, resigned in disgrace, and the scandal helped bring down the government.

Brian Krzanich. Intel's CEO resigned in 2018 after a past consensual relationship with an employee came to light. Running a chip giant doesn't come with an exemption.

According to recent reports, jeff Bezos. His 2019 divorce after 25 years of marriage sent roughly 4% of Amazon, worth about $38 billion at the time, to MacKenzie Scott. Bezos kept his job, married Lauren Sánchez, and is still one of the richest men alive. But it was the most expensive breakup in history.

The pattern is clear. Kingdoms, careers, and fortunes are rebuildable. However, once you find the one, you will do anything to get them.

Industry observers note that remember Indecent Proposal from 1993? Robert Redford’s billionaire character offers a struggling couple, played by Demi Moore and Woody Harrelson, $1 million for one night with the wife. They take the deal. Their marriage nearly implodes.

According to recent reports, the couple discovered they had a price, and it wasn’t that high. But they badly underestimated what they were selling.

Meanwhile, the billionaire could buy the night. He couldn’t buy her heart. He had everything except the one thing he actually wanted.

Swap Redford for any modern tech billionaire and the lesson holds. Money can buy almost anything. Except the feeling of being genuinely loved.

The lack of money is a solvable problem.

It has been revealed that plenty of regular people have become millionaires this way. The formula is public.

Sources indicate that there is no formula for love. You can do everything right and still never meet the one. And even if you do, roughly 40% of first marriages in America end in divorce. Finding love involves tremendous luck. Keeping it is work.

Recent findings suggest that you can always make another dollar. You can't always make another soulmate.

It has been revealed that in 2023, the U.S. Surgeon General declared loneliness an epidemic. About half of American adults report feeling lonely, and the health impact of social disconnection was compared to smoking up to 15 cigarettes a day.

The FIRE crowd isn't immune. Early retirement can be isolating. Your friends are at work. Your identity is gone. And if you're married, there's a specific trap worth sharing.

FIRE is better when both partners retire and experience freedom together. Not when one spouse is slaving away while the other is kicking back. Resentment will surely kick in.

Yes, I get it. Some men’s egos still need protecting when their wives are bringing home the sashimi. But men need to get over themselves. Women now make up the majority of college students, and plenty of them will out-earn their husbands.

It has been revealed that I left banking in 2012. My wife kept working until 2015 when she negotiated her own severance. For almost three years, I was the guy at home while she commuted.

If you're planning FIRE, initiative a joint exit. Life is better this way.

Industry observers note that 1) A high-value spouse may need more respect just to break even. If your partner is successful, attractive, or powerful, the world is constantly praising them. Next to all that adoration, treating them normally at home can inadvertently feel like a lack of respect, or even disrespect. So you may have to deliberately show more appreciation than feels natural just to run in place.

2) Everything gets taken for granted. Eat Kobe beef every day and you’ll get sick of it. In FIRE land, wake up without an alarm clock every day and you’ll take that for granted too. The antidote is voluntary discomfort. Scrub your own toilets after a massive investment win. Take a part-time consulting gig a 40-minute bus ride away that makes you take orders from a micromanager. Practice fasting for at least 18 hours once a month if you have access to unlimited food. Doing uncomfortable things on purpose helps you appreciate the people you already have.

Sources indicate that 3) Privacy is priceless. When you’re private, you can fix your mistakes without the whole world watching. Being known in your small circle for something good is great. Being famous means millions of strangers have opinions about who you are. Respond to all of them and you’ll never have peace of mind. Embrace being a rich nobody.

In a recent development, whatever the full truth turns out to be, this whole situation is sad. Sad for Lori and their adult children. Sad for Jensen and his legacy. Disappointing for Nvidia’s tens of thousands of employees and shareholders like me. And a blow for America, given we’re in a global AI race.

Recent findings suggest that relationships are hard. They require constant work and attentiveness. Forty years of marriage doesn’t buy you immunity. If anything, it makes it easier to stop paying attention.

Industry observers note that if there’s one silver lining, it’s that this story may help bring the left and the right together on maintaining our lead in AI. AI spending has been one of the biggest drivers of U.S. economic growth. If post-midterm infighting causes us to lose the race, we could sink the economy along with it.

Recent findings suggest that if someone with that much money and goodwill was allegedly willing to risk throwing it away, you can’t really blame people for their emotions and their desire to be loved. We’re all human.

Besides a basic amount of financial security, I hope my kids will find someone who will support, love, and cherish them. I would rather my kids find that person than be rich.

According to recent reports, money can help protect them after I’m gone. But money can’t hug them after a bad day, sit with them in a hospital waiting room, or celebrate their wins with them. Knowing they each have someone like that is what will let me rest easy. That’s when I’ll know my kids will be OK.

In a recent development, then I hope they never take that person for granted. Because the odds say they will, just like most of us take for granted the water we drink and the air we breathe.

Readers, do you agree that making money is easier than finding love? Would you take the $1 million in Indecent Proposal, or $2.2 million in today's dollars? If you've achieved FIRE, did you and your spouse exit together, or did one of you keep working, and how did that affect your relationship? And if you had $140+ billion, how would you ever know if someone loved you for you?

According to recent reports, if you're a worried parent, I'm diligently working on my upcoming book out in Fall 2027, Your Kids Will Be OK: Smart Money Decisions For Parents In An Uncertain World, published by Portfolio Penguin. It's about raising capable, resilient kids and making solid money decisions so they have a real shot at independence, and at a good life.

In a recent development, you can’t buy love, but you can protect it. If your family depends on your income, term life insurance is one of the most loving financial moves you can make.

My wife and I each got matching 20-year term policies through Policygenius after shopping around for months. It took far less time than I expected, and we sleep better knowing our kids would be OK if the unthinkable happened. Check out Policygenius to compare quotes from top insurers for free.

Stocks can swing 20% on a single headline. Real estate tends to move more slowly, generate rental income, and give you something tangible to own. That’s why real estate has been a core part of my net worth for over 23 years, and it helps me sleep better when the stock market gets volatile.

If you want real estate exposure without the hassle of being a landlord, check out Fundrise. It invests in a diversified portfolio of private real estate across the Sunbelt, including residential and industrial properties, and is expanding into data centers as demand for computing power grows. You can start with just $10.

Money is the easier problem to solve, and I’ve been helping readers solve it since 2009. Join 60,000+ others and get my free weekly newsletter here. I share what I’m seeing and doing with my own money, plus the lessons on family, freedom, and life that don’t fit neatly into a spreadsheet.

You'll Always Regret Sacrificing Love For Money.

#149387. Breaking: Karl Bushby Reaches Mother's House, Ending 28-Year Journey Around the World

Breaking: Karl Bushby Reaches Mother's House, Ending 28-Year Journey Around the World

📅 02 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3358 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that “This is absolute madness,” said a happy Karl Bushby, as hundreds of people welcomed him home in a civic ceremony in his hometown of Hull, England.
  • The reunion with his mother a couple of hours later was equally public, as the pair were surrounded by TV cameras and hundreds of well-wishers.
  • Recent findings suggest that when Karl Bushby quietly set off from the southern tip of South America on November 1 of that year, it was very different.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that “This is absolute madness,” said a happy Karl Bushby, as hundreds of people welcomed him home in a civic ceremony in his hometown of Hull, England. In a scene that couldn’t be more different from the past 28 years that he has spent walking around the world, Bushby stood underneath a giant Welcome Home Karl sign, made an appreciative speech, then begged off to continue walking the final few steps to his mother’s house, which he left back in 1998.

The reunion with his mother a couple of hours later was equally public, as the pair were surrounded by TV cameras and hundreds of well-wishers.

Recent findings suggest that when Karl Bushby quietly set off from the southern tip of South America on November 1 of that year, it was very different. Bushby was 29 years old. He is now 57. When he began, he had around $500 in his pocket, a two-wheeled cart loaded with supplies, and an idea that most people would have dismissed as a fantasy. He was going to walk home to Hull, England, without using any transport. He would not return to the UK until he could do so on foot. He expected the expedition to take about 12 years. Instead, it has taken 28.

It has been revealed that bushby has spent more than 10,000 days and 50,000km pursuing that single objective. The Goliath Expedition has become one of the longest and most unusual human-powered adventures in modern exploration, and he is nervous about it ending. Speaking to The Washington Post as he approached home, he said: “My purpose and reason for living is about to end. It’s going to be difficult…trying to blend back into a society that you just don’t know anymore.”.

Through Chile’s Atacama Desert. Photo: Karl Bushby.

Recent findings suggest that while serving with the Parachute Regiment, Bushby received a birthday card from his father, Keith, who had served in the British Army. In it was a story about special forces soldiers debating whether it was possible to walk from London to Latest York via the Bering Strait. Looking at a world map, Bushby began tracing the route himself.

But rather than stopping at New York, he extended the line south through the Americas, all the way to the tip of Chile. The result was an expedition that would take him from the southernmost reaches of South America back to his home in England.

“That was the moment the hairs on the back of your neck stand up,” he told GQ Magazine. “You think, well, that’s it.” He did some calculations, created a timeline on the “back of a beer mat,” and estimated the journey would take him 12 years. From that point, Bushby demonstrated nothing but determination. At the start, most people doubted it was even possible. That only made him more certain that he wanted to try.

He gave himself two rules. The first was that he could not use any transportation, even self-propelled vehicles like bicycles or kayaks, to advance the expedition. The second was that he could not return to the UK until he had completed the walk. Those rules sound simple. In practice, they created multiple logistical nightmares and affected almost every aspect of his life.

2001, the Darien Gap. Photo: Karl Bushby.

It has been revealed that bushby left Punta Arenas, Chile, with his equipment loaded onto a cart he calls The Beast. He was not an elite endurance athlete embarking on a carefully funded and organized expedition. He was a young former paratrooper with a few hundred dollars, a rough line on a map, and limited resources. He had no supporters or funding, and relied on gas station food or what locals gave him.

“The first years, you’re living the boys’ adventure dream, and it’s great,” he told The New York Times, “and then it really becomes a grind.”.

Industry observers note that the first few years took him north through the Americas, including multiple conflict zones. In Peru, he was attacked by a mob; in Colombia, he floated down the crocodile-laden Atrato River to avoid being spotted by armed men. Then he faced the Darien Gap, that infamously dangerous stretch between Colombia and Panama, ruled by drug and human smugglers, that almost all adventurers skirt around.

Industry observers note that eventually, he reached Panama. But emerging from the jungle did not mean he was free to continue. After crossing a restricted border zone without the necessary visa, he was detained for 18 days.

Sources indicate that after making his way through the Americas, Bushby eventually finished crossing the U.S., where he had picked up a few sponsorships, and reached Alaska. The next major obstacle, and the one that catapulted his journey into world news, was the Bering Strait, the stretch of water separating North America from Russia.

According to recent reports, north America. Photo: Karl Bushby.

According to recent reports, the Arctic had already given Bushby a taste of its dangers. During the Alaskan stage of the expedition, he was rescued by helicopter after becoming stranded on an ice floe that broke away from the coast and drifted out to sea, and had a standoff with a polar bear. He knew how risky the Bering Strait crossing would be.

Sources indicate that in March 2006, Bushby and French adventurer Dimitri Kieffer spent 14 days crossing the Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia on foot. With 90kg sleds, they traveled across the shifting ice in temperatures that fell to around -30˚C, against the prevailing winds as the ice moved beneath them.

Wearing dry suits, they had to swim at points through the icy, slushy water. “All night long, you’re just listening to the grinding, and the ice is just like screaming,” he told The New York Times. “We actually had to evacuate the tent during the night because the thing started to break apart beneath us.”.

They made it across, achieving a rare crossing of one of the world’s most formidable natural barriers. But reaching Russia did not mean the difficulties were over. Russian authorities detained the pair for entering the country without the required permission. They faced the possibility of deportation.

Sources indicate that crossing the Bering Strait. Photo: Karl Bushby.

Sources indicate that russia would consume years of Bushby’s life. He had to leave the country every 90 days because his tourist visa allowed him to stay in Russia for only 90 of every 180 days. Then in 2008, his journey came to a standstill. He lost sponsorship and could not travel to Russia for a few years. In 2011, he resumed his trek, again in 90-day stints. Then in 2012, he was denied a further visa, and in 2013, he received a five-year entry ban from Russia.

Here, Bushby responded with an extraordinary protest. He walked approximately 5,000km from Los Angeles to the Russian Embassy in Washington, D.C., hoping to draw attention to his predicament and secure the paperwork he needed to continue.

The years of delay exposed another unusual aspect of the expedition. Bushby’s rules did not mean he had to remain indefinitely in the country where he was stuck. Nor did they prevent him from using transport for journeys unrelated to advancing his route home. However, he couldn’t fly back to the UK during these hiatuses.

When visas, funding, or political restrictions prevented him from continuing, he could fly elsewhere, take a break, and wait until circumstances allowed him to resume. But he could not use that flight to skip a section of the route. Whenever he returned, he had to pick up from the exact point where he had stopped. Most of the time, he decamped to Mexico. Its lower cost of living made it a practical place to wait. He also spent time in the United States.

Bushby and Dimitri Kieffer, 2006. Photo: Karl Bushby.

The distinction mattered enormously to the expedition. Bushby could board a plane to escape a logistical dead end, but when he returned to the route, he had to pick up where he had stopped. He could not simply fly over the awkward section and resume walking on the other side.

Industry observers note that the arrangement might seem to stretch the definition of walking around the world. But for Bushby, it was the only way to maintain his two original rules without spending years of his life waiting at a closed border. Some visa delays took years to resolve. And the longer the journey continued, the harder it became to predict when, or even whether, it would end. Getting across Russia alone took almost 10 years.

He lived cheaply but still needed money to survive on this near-endless journey. Some of it came from the sponsorships he eventually acquired. During what sounded like a particularly low point 15 years ago, on one of his hiatuses in Mexico while trying to overcome another logistical hurdle on his journey, he told Backpacker magazine:.

I’m 42 years old and I’m broke and I’m homeless. I’m a professional parasite. I’m a professional hobo. I’m sleeping on other people’s couches. I’m 42 years old, and I have to walk other people’s dogs, just so they’ll feed me. My job is picking up dog shit!

Recent findings suggest that the passage of time is one of the most striking aspects of Bushby’s story. His expedition began in an era before smartphones, Instagram, and the expectation of sharing every stage of an adventure online. The young man who left Chile in 1998 could never have imagined that nearly three decades later, people around the world would be following his progress toward his childhood home. The fact that so many people are following it still baffles Bushby.

In a recent development, while Bushby was away, life continued for the people he had left behind. His son, Adam, grew up, and his family had to get on with their lives without him. Adam was eight when he set off. He is now 36, with a family of his own, including a 12-year-old daughter whom Bushby has never met.

In a recent development, when his dad started the walk, Adam didn’t fully understand what was going on, or know how to explain it to people who asked. Over the years, they have tried to stay in touch and maintain some kind of relationship. At 14, Adam flew to Alaska to see his dad. It was six years after the expedition began and a turning point for him in accepting what Bushby was doing. “I did feel a bit awkward because at that point I didn’t really know my dad,” he told GQ Magazine.

They later spent 10 days walking together as part of a National Geographic documentary project. Adam described the experience as surreal, suddenly stepping into his father’s world. They have spoken regularly since, but as Adam put it: “[His] life went this way, and I went that way, two separate routes.”.

In various interviews, Adam has explained that he had nothing against his father’s ambition, that he respects what he has done and is very proud of him. But also that growing up without him had been difficult.

Recent findings suggest that karl Bushby has not seen other members of his family for years. He met Adam when he stepped out of the water after crossing the English Channel back to England, but he has not seen his mother in over a decade, even though he will be living with her once he arrives back at his childhood home. He recognizes how difficult the situation will be and that it is due to his choices over the last 30 years.

“The relationship between me and my son is good, but there’s a lot to resolve there,” he told GQ Magazine. “I’ve got a granddaughter I’ve never seen, and then dear old mother, Lord. I have to live with my mother now. I’m going from a global adventure to living with my mother in a basement at 57. This is going to be a challenge.”.

Life on the road has often been lonely, but Bushby has seen kindness and hospitality in every corner of the globe. “I’ve been welcomed in by the poorest of the poor,” he told The Washington Post. “I’ve met 99.9999% of the very best of humanity. Every culture, every country, has been the same response.”.

Industry observers note that he has also had two significant romantic relationships during the expedition. He spent around seven years with a Colombian woman. Later, he had a three-year relationship with a woman from Japan. He met both while on the expedition, and it was also the reason both broke down.

After finally getting across Russia, Bushby continued through Mongolia, where he joined with other adventurers, including Angela Maxwell, to trek across the Gobi Desert with camels. After 1,130km and several disagreements, the group went their separate ways, and Busby continued into China by himself. In 2018, he crossed Kazakhstan and then made his way through Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. Once again, visa issues ground the journey to a standstill. He could not get into Iran.

At the same time, the world was struck down by the pandemic. More years of waiting in Mexico began, even though Bushby still had a substantial distance to cover. Eventually, in 2022, he was on the move again. Once again joined by Angela Maxwell, he did something he had never intended doing during the expedition — swimming across the Caspian Sea.

Recent findings suggest that visa challenges and geopolitics meant he was unable to cross into Iran. So he came up with a new initiative. He and Maxwell went back to Uzbekistan and took a different route. They walked across the Kyzylkum Desert until they reached the Caspian Sea. A self-proclaimed terrible swimmer, he was completely outside of his comfort zone. Wearing a wetsuit and flotation equipment, he described his floating-and-swimming hybrid as floatimming. It might not have been the most elegant crossing, but after 32 days at sea, 27 of which he was swimming with Maxwell and two Azerbaijani swimmers in very choppy waters, he completed the 288km swim.

Back on solid ground, his next job was to get across Azerbaijan and into Turkey. Here, he hit a huge milestone. He crossed the Bosphorus Bridge on May 2, 2025. This meant he was back in Europe for the first time since he started walking.

Recent findings suggest that the remaining distance to Britain was comparatively short, but the final stages were not straightforward. Once again, visa restrictions were the thorn in his side. Limited to traveling for 90 days at a time before having to leave Europe, he continued to use Mexico as a base as he waited for his 90 days to reset and tackled the remaining distance in short stretches.

He made it through Turkey, Bulgaria, and Romania before confronting the next issue. Bushby always knew one of the logistical challenges would be getting from France to England. He started trying to pull a plan together. Unsurprisingly, for someone who has walked across the world, his goal was to cross it via the Channel Tunnel. The issue was that this was forbidden. He had hoped to use their service tunnel, but his request was denied.

Karl Bushby speaks at a civic ceremony in Hull, England earlier today. Photo: YouTube.

As he continued walking through Hungary and Austria, he attempted to appeal the decision, reaching out to anyone who might help, to no avail. “We have carefully considered his request and explored a range of possible options. In this instance, regretfully, we are unable to accommodate Mr Bushby’s wishes,” a spokesperson for the Eurotunnel told the BBC. This meant the only alternative was to get back into the water and swim the Channel.

Industry observers note that still walking, he had made it to Germany. Then he picked his way across Belgium and France, all the while decamping to Mexico, Canada, or the U.S. every 90 days, and trying to piece together a plan for swimming the Channel. This proved to be another headache regarding permissions.

Recent findings suggest that french rules stop anyone swimming the Channel from France to Britain. He thought he had been granted an exemption, but in September, he learned that was not the case. After much negotiation, he finally got the go-ahead. On October 5, Bushby finally landed back on British soil at Shakespeare Beach near Dover after swimming the English Channel.

In a recent development, the crossing took three days. He spent around 20 hours in the water, spent the nights on a safety vessel, and dropped back into the water at his last-known position each morning.

It has been revealed that after 28 years abroad, he was finally back in the country he had left in 1998. But rather than feeling joy, he told The New York Times he felt a real sense of loss. After three decades on the road, the prospect of just 400km to go was hugely daunting. “I’m about to lose my purpose for living,” he noted. “It’s about to abruptly end.”.

In a recent development, he is nervous about what comes next and reintegrating into a society he no longer knows. He is considering retraining as a teacher, as he loved giving talks in schools as he walked.

Sources indicate that one substantial question is why Bushby has become so celebrated. He is not the first person to have attempted a long-distance walk around the world. Other adventurers have spent years traveling between countries, crossing continents on foot, or undertaking journeys without motorized transport, but Bushby has singularly captured the world’s attention.

It has been revealed that karl Bushby, back turned, leaves the civic ceremony to walk the last few steps to his mother’s house. Photo: YouTube.

It has been revealed that it might be the particular combination of his rules, or the fact that his objective is immediately understandable. He left home, and he is walking back. There is no complicated scientific mission to explain, no specialized equipment that the public needs to understand, and no obscure record category he is aiming for. The simplicity of it gives the story an almost fable-like quality, even though the journey was not simple at all.

In a recent development, with just two rules, the expedition is relatively easy to follow. Every delay matters because Bushby cannot simply skip ahead. He is forced to wait or find another solution when something blocks his route. The question becomes how he will get around it without abandoning his principles.

In a recent development, then there is the sheer amount of time it has taken. People who first encountered Bushby’s expedition in their twenties are now well into middle age themselves. Initially, there were no updates on social media. Instead, there was the odd news article that cropped up every few years about the same man, still walking across the world. A story that seemed like an ambitious adventure morphed into an entire adult life on the road.

Bushby has not necessarily made the journey look enjoyable. His progress has depended as much, if not more, on navigating bureaucracy and finding support as on putting one foot in front of the other. Despite it all, he continued.

As the journey has hit an era where we can follow an adventurer’s progress in real time, every obstacle and milestone has renewed interest in the question that has followed Bushby for 28 years: Will he actually make it home?

Recent findings suggest that now that he has to confront a latest question: How do you cope with coming home after three decades? “I will have to figure out who I am again. What is the meaning to it all? How do I find that meaning and purpose? How do I fill that hole I’m suddenly going to find myself in?” he told the BBC in the days before the expected end of the expedition. “I think the old adage goes…the only thing worse than a man who can’t fulfill his dreams is a man who’s fulfilled his dreams…because then what?”.

  • In a recent development, no cyclone seems enough to deter the Russian team on Everest for very long.
  • Sources indicate that the climbers’ latest foray up Everest’s West Ridge route.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that the second cyclone to hit Nepal’s mountains this season caused heavy snowfall last weekend, but its briefer stay has affected climbers and trekkers less. As the sun returned this afternoon, fresh snow hampered smaller teams on 6,000m and 7,000m peaks, but the highly supported expeditions on Ama Dablam are proceeding with barely a hitch.

In a recent development, no cyclone seems enough to deter the Russian team on Everest for very long. Leader Andrei Vasiliev told us yesterday from Kathmandu that he, Sergey Kondrashkin, and Vitaly Shipilov will return to the mountain in one or two days. The trio is well aware of the challenge they face on Everest’s West Ridge, completely alone and without oxygen.

Sources indicate that the climbers’ latest foray up Everest’s West Ridge route. Photo: Andrei Vasiliev.

Industry observers note that vasiliev mentioned he is under some pressure due to unidentified “unsolved matters” but still determined to tackle the climb. In his own words:.

Sources indicate that we know what needs to be done; the path is clear, and we must attempt to follow it. We’ve fallen ill. A massive amount of snow has fallen. You adapt quickly to new conditions. Once we’re back in the snow, the cold, and the cramped tent, it will feel as though things were never any other way.

Recent findings suggest that the fresh snow dump has thwarted some teams attempting Baruntse (7,129m) in the Khumbu. Jan McManus of Ireland was among them, and he has called off his expedition after failing to reach Camp 1 due to deep snow:.

It is unclear whether other climbers on the peak may still be trying. There were six large teams totaling 65 foreign climbers with permits for Baruntse.

Recent findings suggest that on Himlung (7,126m), teams hurried to summit and get down and safely away before the cyclone hit. During the previous snowstorm at the end of September, a massive avalanche buried Base Camp, killing 16 staff members. Despite the tragedy, one of the deadliest in Nepal’s mountaineering history, the peak remained open, and guided teams came in large numbers to the mountain a couple of weeks after the accident. A total of 130 foreigners had permits. Teams summited on October 25 and 26, and then left the area.

Ama Dablam Base Camp is also covered in snow, but the commercial teams will nevertheless resume climbing soon. According to Jana Schneider of Germany, climbing with 14 Peaks Expeditions, a Sherpa team is on its way to reopen those sections where fresh snow has buried the ropes. “If all goes well, my summit push begins Nov 4 until Nov 6,” she wrote.

So far, 410 foreigners have applied for a permit to climb Ama Dablam. A Sherpa team first fixed the route on October 17, and dozens have summited since then. Despite the break forced by bad weather over the weekend, summits should continue throughout November.

It has been revealed that one climber has perished on the mountain so far, and there have been some close calls. Paul Clarke of Australia and Xenia Santha of Hungary climbed Ama Dablam after attempting Dhaulagiri earlier this season. Their summit push was delayed as they found a 25-year-old climber in a serious situation at Camp 2. Santha and Clarke, who climbed without Sherpa support, gave the climber dexamethasone, spent the night with him, and helped organize an emergency airlift for the following morning. They continued to the summit one day later.

A high camp on Ama Dablam. Photo: Xenia Shanta.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Explorersweb ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: New Route Attempt on Lunag Ri Falls Just Short of Summit

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (633 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, between October 23 and 27, Alexander Parfenov and Alexander Semenov of Russia opened a demanding new route on 6,895m Lunag Ri in the Rolwaling Himal on the Nepal-Tibet border.
  • Recent findings suggest that the pair climbed a previously unexplored southeast-facing buttress of the Lunag Ri massif.
  • It has been revealed that they placed a piton on the final part of the pillar and began rappelling from there, reaching the base of the wall on October 28, according to gore-ljudje.net.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, between October 23 and 27, Alexander Parfenov and Alexander Semenov of Russia opened a demanding new route on 6,895m Lunag Ri in the Rolwaling Himal on the Nepal-Tibet border. They turned back short of the summit, which some sources list as 6,907m.

Recent findings suggest that the pair climbed a previously unexplored southeast-facing buttress of the Lunag Ri massif. The line would have ended on the southeast summit. It involved mixed and rock climbing to M6, aid sections of A2–A3, ice up to WI5–WI6 in places, and long stretches of steep snow with limited protection.

It has been revealed that they placed a piton on the final part of the pillar and began rappelling from there, reaching the base of the wall on October 28, according to gore-ljudje.net. The duo turned back short of the summit due to a coming storm and health issues. The complex summit area — multiple closely linked peaks and ridge features — also left some uncertainty about how close they came to the main summit.

Even without summiting, this was a significant exploration of a major, unclimbed feature on a remote peak.

It has been revealed that the upcoming line opened by the Parfenov and Semenov. Photo: Alexander Parfenov.

Lunag Ri, the highest peak in the Lunag massif, has long stood as one of Nepal’s highest unclimbed summits. Early attention focused on the broader massif after Joe Puryear and David Gottlieb made the first ascent of the neighboring 6,778m Jobo Rinjang via its South Face in 2009.

In the same year, a Swiss-led team under Stephane Schaffter attempted lines in the area, including approaches to Lunag I, though their claims about summits on the massif were later met with skepticism in the American Alpine Journal.

Sources indicate that in the autumn of 2010, a French team that included Max Belleville, Mathieu Detrie, Mathieu Maynadier, and Sebastien Ratel climbed the southeast face of Lunag Ri. Their route, Close the Door (1,200 m, IV/5 F5), was completed in a three-day alpine-style push with two bivouacs. They reached a distinct southeast top (6,812m to 6,830m) on the long ridge connecting Lunag I to Jobo Rinjang. By this time, they were exhausted and did not continue the short remaining traverse to the higher main summit. This remains the only major completed route on the Lunag I massif before the first ascent of the true summit.

In a recent development, from the recent climb on Lunag Ri. Photo: Alexander Parfenov.

Sources indicate that attention then shifted to the west ridge and southwest face of the main peak. In November 2015, Conrad Anker and David Lama’s alpine-style attempt reached a high point roughly 300m below the summit before retreating due to the unexpected complexity of the ridge.

They returned in 2016 to try a similar line. On the first day, at about 5,800m, Anker suffered a heart attack and was evacuated by helicopter. Lama subsequently continued alone on a variation that moved farther right onto an icefield. He established two bivouacs and pushed 50m higher than the previous year’s high point before turning around 250m shy of the summit.

It has been revealed that in late October 2018, Lama returned solo. Over three days (October 23-25), with two bivouacs, he climbed the southwest face and northwest/west ridge (1,500m of vertical gain, terrain to 90°). He moved mostly ropeless, with limited self-belaying on the harder mixed sections. Lama negotiated the previously unclimbed headwall and made the final exposed traverse onto the main summit.

This was the first ascent of Lunag Ri’s highest point. He descended largely by rappelling down the line of ascent. Lama was awarded a Piolet d’Or for this solo first ascent of Lunag Ri.

From the recent climb on Lunag Ri. Photo: Alexander Parfenov.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Indian mountaineer and adventurer Shekhar Bordoloi has just started a solo expedition down the Brahmaputra River.
  • This won’t be Bordoloi’s first time down the river.
  • In a recent development, bordoloi on a previous raft expedition on the Brahmaputra.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Indian mountaineer and adventurer Shekhar Bordoloi has just started a solo expedition down the Brahmaputra River. He set off on a homemade on a bamboo raft from the Dhola–Sadiya Bridge on November 1 and aims to finish at Dhubri, 891km later. The route covers the entire Brahmaputra within India and should take 22 to 25 days in all. The river begins in Tibet and continues beyond India into Bangladesh, covering 2,900km in all.

This won’t be Bordoloi’s first time down the river. In 2020, he and two friends took a similar bamboo raft down a 400km section of the Brahmaputra. Earlier, in 2015, Bordoloi was one of 11 who tackled another part of the river over 11 days under the auspices of the Assam Mountaineering Association. This expedition, however, will test his endurance, pitting him against river conditions for longer, and with less support, than ever before.

In a recent development, bordoloi on a previous raft expedition on the Brahmaputra. This raft took Bordoloi and friends from the world’s largest river island, Umananda, to its smallest, Majuli. Photo: Shekhar Bordoloi/Instagram.

Bordoloi’s raft was hand-built from bamboo poles carefully lashed together over several days. Such craft are a traditional way of navigating rivers across the region, and are still used by local communities for fishing and transportation.

Sources indicate that though the river can be temperamental, Bordoloi’s first two days have been relatively calm, taking him down the Lohit, one of the Brahmaputra’s many tributaries and channels. Navigating the complex river system alone will be a challenge. The Brahmaputra is one of the largest river systems in India, the ninth-largest in the world by discharge, and is prone to flooding and powerful currents.

Recent findings suggest that but according to Bordoloi, those obscure, winding corridors are at the heart of this project. Many sections of the river remain underexplored, and he believes there is hidden potential for the people in his home region of Assam. If he can map routes for river tourism and model environmentally responsible river navigation through those routes, he hopes to draw attention to this important riverine ecosystem and the economic opportunities for the people living along it.

According to recent reports, the logistical challenges of a long expedition will further complicate progress. On previous expeditions, Bordoloi traveled with minimal supplies or no food at all, relying entirely on foraging and knowledge of the natural landscape. But this adventure will take over twice as long and may put those skills to their limits.

Bordoloi is documenting his daily progress on Facebook and Instagram.

Rental property is how I broke free. The rent from my San Francisco properties was one of the foundations that let me leave banking in 2012 at age 34. Without it, I’d probably still be waking up at 5 am to get to the office by 5:45 am and leaving after 6 pm.

I’ve been a landlord since 2005. I’ve had good tenants, great tenants, and tenants who refused to take their trash with them during the final walkthrough.

Industry observers note that I’m forever grateful for owning rental property. But the older I get, the less I enjoy being a landlord.

It has been revealed that it’s not the math. It’s the tenant headaches, the turnover, and the maintenance. The 9 pm leaky faucet text. The final walkthrough that starts 30 minutes late. At 49 with two young kids, my time is worth more and my patience is worth less.

Industry observers note that 2025 tested me with three tenant turnovers. Each one meant a deposit to return, walls to paint, a vacancy to absorb, and a new tenant to find. Not long after, I sold one of my rentals. Earning 100% passive income feels better.

But selling also feels like giving up. Owning rental property is a war of attrition. The longer you hold, the more wealth you usually build. Hold until you pass, and your heirs may get a step-up in basis that wipes out the capital gains entirely.

Selling isn’t free either. Commissions, transfer taxes, capital gains, and depreciation recapture take a big bite. Then you lose the rent check and future appreciation on a property you’ll likely never buy back at the same price.

According to recent reports, semi-passive income you can live with beats optimized income you can’t wait to dump. You can’t automate away a difficult tenant or a burst pipe. But you can automate a lot of what surrounds them. That’s where Baselane comes in.

Sources indicate that for 21 years, I’ve tracked my rental finances with a spreadsheet and emails. Old school. With three rentals left in San Francisco, it kind of works. I know my numbers, more or less.

But add another property, an LLC, a partner, or a short-term rental, and a DIY system starts to creak. Debits and credits slip through the cracks.

Four rentals is why I sold one last year. I couldn’t comfortably handle all the maintenance and management myself. And I didn’t want to pay a property manager 10% of rent or more to do a worse job than me.

Since Baselane is sponsoring this post, I opened a free account for one of my SF rentals to see how it compares. Here’s what stood out.

It has been revealed that baselane is a free business bank account, bookkeeping software, and rent collection app rolled into one login, built for landlords. Think business checking plus QuickBooks plus Venmo for rent, except it knows what a Schedule E is.

Recent findings suggest that banking and books live in the same system, so you never reconcile. Baselane is a fintech, not a bank. Deposits are held at Thread Bank, Member FDIC.

Industry observers note that one of the first rules of landlording is to keep rental money separate from personal money. One of the second rules is that it gets messy fast once you own more than one property.

In a recent development, with Baselane, you can open unlimited checking and savings accounts under one login. One per property, one per LLC, one for reserves, however you actually run your portfolio. There are no monthly maintenance fees and no minimum balances, which matters once you're running a handful of accounts.

In a recent development, you can also concern physical and virtual debit cards with spending limits. If you pay contractors, cleaners, or a handyman, you can hand someone a card capped at, say, $1,500 for materials instead of fronting cash and chasing receipts.

Industry observers note that the reserve accounts earn interest. Currently 2.88%. Letting a five-figure repair reserve sit in a checking account earning nothing is a donation to your bank.

If you try it, start with one property. Move its rent and its bills over, get comfortable, then decide about the rest.

Sources indicate that plenty of banks let you open separate accounts. What's different here is that every transaction gets tagged to a property and a Schedule E category as it happens.

Sources indicate that here's why that matters. Before my old Marina tenants moved in, I spent about $2,500 and many hours fixing up the yard. They agreed to hire a gardener twice a month. They never did. Before they moved out, I paid my landscaper $1,400 including materials to restore it, plus two days of my own labor.

It has been revealed that those are deductible repair and maintenance expenses. But only if you record them against the right property and can find the receipts a year later. With one property, I can do that myself. With five, it becomes a part-time job.

Sources indicate that on the Smart initiative, you set rules once, like “payments to my landscaper go to the SF rental under Repairs,” and an AI assistant handles the rest. You can snap a photo of a receipt and it matches it to the transaction.

This is the part that speaks to my real pain point: tenant headaches. It is also my favorite reason for using Baselane.

Industry observers note that I rented my Marina house to five tenants from 2015 to 2017 for about $8,200 a month. The lease charged a $250 late fee after the 4th. Rent was late eight times in 24 months. I waived the fee every single time.

In a recent development, that’s $2,000 I left on the table because I’m a softie who dislikes confrontation. Their method of paying was walking into my bank branch and depositing directly into my account. One July 4th weekend, rent revealed up on the 10th. That’s difficult to deal with when my mortgage is due by the 5th of each month, resulting in cash flow issues.

Industry observers note that that awkwardness wore me down. In 2017, I sold the Marina house for about $2.75 million to simplify my life.

Sources indicate that thanks to the AI boom pushing San Francisco prices higher, that house is likely worth $800,000 to $1 million more today. Sure, I reinvested the proceeds, so the true opportunity cost is lower. But it still stings.

If I’d had a system to collect rent, send reminders, and enforce late fees without me playing bad cop, I would have held on. Selling out of fatigue can be one of the most expensive decisions a landlord makes.

That’s what Baselane does. Invoices, reminders, and late fees go out on schedule. Tenants can pay by ACH or card and set up autopay. Software doesn’t feel guilty enforcing a lease you both signed. Ultimately, Baselane removes friction which increases a rental property owner’s ability to hold on and build more wealth.

According to recent reports, after 21 years, I've also learned that 99% of tenants want as little contact with their landlord as possible. The feeling is mutual. A system that runs rent in the background means fewer awkward conversations, and fewer awkward conversations means a happier landlord who's less tempted to sell.

Recent findings suggest that two catches. Tenants who pay by card pay a 3.49% fee, so steer them to ACH. And if your current rent collection works fine, then great. Baselane's value is rent, banking, and books living in one place.

Recent findings suggest that if you run short-term rentals, payouts from Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com can take several business days to clear at a normal bank. Across multiple listings, that's a constant gap between money earned and money available.

In a recent development, baselane offers faster payouts when you use it as your deposit account on booking platforms, with each listing feeding its own account. Next-day payouts are available for free consumers.

A healthy bank balance doesn't mean a property is performing. You might have a big repair coming, insurance up 20%, or expenses sitting in the wrong account.

According to recent reports, I recently ran the numbers on my San Francisco rental for a post on whether to raise the rent when tenants strike it rich. Rent is $10,250 a month, roughly $1,250 below market, because I honor a three-year rent schedule capped at about 3% a year. One vacant month wipes out about eight months of that discount. And a 2.5% annual increase only covers about 80% of my rising insurance and basic maintenance costs.

Industry observers note that I know those numbers because I track them myself. Most landlords never sit down and run them.

Recent findings suggest that baselane builds income, expense, cash flow, and net operating income reports for each property or your whole portfolio, because every transaction is already tagged. No building spreadsheets from scratch.

In a recent development, with one rental and a spreadsheet you trust, you may not need this. With several properties or LLCs, it's the difference between knowing and guessing whether a property is worth keeping.

Industry observers note that tax season is where sloppy books come back to bite. You end up gathering records, digging up receipts, and trying to remember what a charge from eight months ago was for.

In a recent development, because Baselane categorizes everything during the year, you can download a tax package with Schedule E reports, income statements, and transaction ledgers with receipts for each property and entity. Then you hand it to your CPA or use it to file yourself.

If you have one rental and a DIY system that works, you don't need it. But the Core proposal is free, so there's little downside to trying it.

Baselane makes the most sense if you own several rentals, hold properties in LLCs, or self-manage. Property managers have quoted me fees ranging from 10% to 20% of rent. On a $10,250 rental, a 10% fee is $1,250 a month. Baselane Smart, its premium version is just $20.

That's not apples to apples. Baselane won't fix your garbage disposal or talk to your tenants. But if you self-manage, the administrative half of the job gets a lot lighter.

It has been revealed that it's also worth a look if you're on the fence about selling a rental because you're worn out. Lighten the load before you list it and pay all those exorbitant fees. And if you're buying your next property, set up clean systems first. They're easier to build with one property than to retrofit with five.

Core is free and includes unlimited accounts, debit cards with spend controls, rent collection with automated reminders and late fees, property-level tracking, and the accountant tax package.

Smart is $20 a month with a 30-day free trial and adds AI auto-tagging, receipt matching, auto-transfers to maintain target balances, faster rent deposits, and balance sheet reports.

Industry observers note that compare that to what you may already pay. Some business bank accounts charge $5 to $25 a month in maintenance fees. At $15 a month across five accounts, that's $900 a year just to keep them open. Baselane charges no maintenance fees, no minimums, and ACH transfers and incoming wires are free.

No product is perfect, and pretending otherwise insults your intelligence.

Rental property helped me break free due to the semi-passive income it generates. But a rental only builds wealth if you can stand to keep owning it.

The headaches that make me want to sell are tenants, turnover, and maintenance. Baselane doesn't make those entirely disappear. What it does is take the money side of landlording, rent collection, late fees, accounts, and records, and put it on autopilot. Less friction overall means more energy for the parts that actually need a human.

My plan going forward is simple. Own fewer, better rentals and make each one as close to passive as possible. Let the private real estate side of my portfolio be 100% passive. And spend the time I save being a full-time dad.

Industry observers note that if I’d had automated rent and late fees with my Marina tenants, I’d have $2,000 more and far fewer awkward conversations. I also might still own the house today. That’s at least an $800,000 lesson in letting small annoyances drive big decisions.

Recent findings suggest that selling a rental is permanent. Making one easier to own isn't.

Sources indicate that if you own rental property and want it to feel a little more passive, check out Baselane here. The Core blueprint is free, so the only cost of trying it is an afternoon.

In a recent development, have you ever sold a rental property because you were tired of managing it, not because the numbers stopped working? Do you regret it? According to recent reports, what should real estate investors look for when choosing a bank? Look for property-specific accounts, integrated rent collection, automated bookkeeping, and tax prep support. Multi-property investors benefit most from platforms that organize transactions by property and entity automatically. Security deposit tracking also helps keep tenant funds clearly separated.

Industry observers note that can real estate investors open a business bank account online? Yes. Digital platforms like Baselane let you open accounts entirely online with no branch visit. Traditional banks may require in-person verification depending on their policies and your business structure.

According to recent reports, do any banking platforms for real estate investors offer high-yield savings? Digital-first platforms generally pay more on savings than traditional banks. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Spanish team is back in Kathmandu after their first ascent of Jugal II via a highly difficult 2,000m route.
  • The peak, northeast of Kathmandu on the Nepal-Tibet border, has been a coveted goal since it opened to climbing teams in 2023.
  • Route topo, including a special mention of Nives Meroi and Romano Benet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Spanish team is back in Kathmandu after their first ascent of Jugal II via a highly difficult 2,000m route. Yet, the climbers insist that the best part of the experience was climbing part of the route with Italians Nives Meroi and Romano Benet. Jugal II was Initiative B for the Italian pair after flooding washed out access to their primary target, Tilicho Peak in the Annapurna region.

The peak, northeast of Kathmandu on the Nepal-Tibet border, has been a coveted goal since it opened to climbing teams in 2023. In the end, it was the skill and smart strategy of Mikel Zabalza, Ruben Perez, and Mikel Saez de Urabain that put them on the unclimbed 6,518m summit after an alpine-style push via the east-southeast face.

Route topo, including a special mention of Nives Meroi and Romano Benet.

The team mentioned that the greatest technical difficulties came high on the route. “From the upper bivouac, the climb goes on pretty vertical mixed terrain, with sections of poor-quality rock,” Zabalza explained. “It’s sustained M5 with some even harder sections, until 6,450m. Then the rest of the way to the summit follows along a 55˚-60˚snow slope.”.

A tough, vertical mixed section. Photo: Mikel Zabalza.

It has been revealed that they reached the summit on October 29, at 4:00 pm. The weather was clear but very cold, with some evening humidity.

Industry observers note that “We made three bivouacs on the route, two on the way up and one more on descent, and all of them were rather precarious,” Mikel Zabalza told ExplorersWeb from Kathmandu. “Luckily, we had a tarp to enlarge them.”.

One of the climbers on the summit of Jugal II. Photo: Mikel Zabalza.

Industry observers note that the Spanish team, all highly experienced alpinists, had been studying the route for months. This was key to their success.

Industry observers note that the situation was different for Benet and Meroi of Italy. Since they had not planned to do Jugal II, their approach to the route was more improvisational. They had no previous information about what they would find. To make matters worse, the third member of the team, Tine Cuder of Slovenia, had to abandon the expedition due to health problems.

According to recent reports, one of the Spanish team’s bivouacs, with a tiny ledge enlarged by a fabric tarp. Photo: Romano Benet.

According to recent reports, there was no competition between the two teams, who happily joined forces for the summit push. However, the Spaniards’ strategy proved essential on the highly steep ramps covered with unstable snow.

It has been revealed that nivel Meroi loaded with bivy gear on highly steep mixed ramps on Jugal II. Photo: Romano Benet.

It has been revealed that “We set off on an adventure, having never seen the mountain before and not knowing what kind of ascent awaited us, but we gave it a try,” Romano Benet reported from Kathmandu. “We decided to turn back to avoid a third bivouac. ”.

The two teams joined forces and were in good spirits on the route. Photo: Romano Benet.

Benet explained that they lacked the necessary gear (specifically, a tarp like Zabalza’s group) to pitch bivvies “on this type of face, where it’s impossible to carve out a ledge.”.

Otherwise, the two groups returned as friends. “Nives and Romano are exceptional people,” Zabalza said.

“We are back from the mountain with new experiences and ideas but, most of all, with three new fantastic friends with whom, hopefully, we will share more adventures in the future,” Romano Benet concluded.

The Spanish team sent us the video below summarizing the climb.

  • Industry observers note that “Even though there are always a lot of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp, this kind of traffic is not usual,” Ngima Sherpa explained.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The image of an endless line of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp this week seemed like deja vu. Why are conga lines similar to the infamous ones filmed every May on Everest’s Hillary Step, now repeating at the base of the mountain? We asked the local trekking guide who shot the video.

Ngima Sherpa of Osprey Adventure explained that this is not the norm, but the delay caused by Cyclone Anwar, which hit Nepal last weekend, has created a huge backlog.

Industry observers note that “Even though there are always a lot of trekkers heading to Everest Base Camp, this kind of traffic is not usual,” Ngima Sherpa explained. “This video was shot on November 1, after three days of continuous snow and rain…During that time, all the trekkers were stuck in Dingboche, which is two trekking stages away from Everest Base Camp.”.

When the weather finally cleared, all those trekkers set off for EBC at the same time, causing heavy traffic on the route from Dingboche to Gorakshep.

The recent cyclone is also the reason why the surroundings are so heavily covered in snow. Usually, the entire trail to Everest Base Camp is dry.

In a recent development, the fresh snow on Nepal’s peaks is having consequences for those planning to summit trekking peaks. Conditions on otherwise straightforward snow slopes have become problematic, as climbers sink into deep, heavy snow.

Satori Adventures had to retreat after swimming in snow on the flanks of Mera Peak, in the Khumbu. “Four to five feet of fresh snow made it impossible to move forward above high camp,” leader Furba Sherpa reported.

Ramesh Gurung noted today that he has retreated from an attempt on 6,119m Lobuche East, another popular Khumbu 6000’er. However, Gurung said he will try again with another group soon.

Conditions will change only as the snow transforms under the dimming sun and freezes in the approaching winter temperatures.

In a recent development, on Ama Dablam, Sherpa climbers struggled to reopen the route to Camp 1 on Tuesday but managed to complete it. The route above Camp 1 follows a steep, mixed ridge with less accumulated snow. Several teams are now on their summit rotations and expect to top out in the next few days.

Sources indicate that tenzing Sherpa of Gokyo Namaste Lodge has shared some useful information for trekkers who plan to cross the huge Ngozumpa Glacier between Gokyo and Dragnag. The recent snowfall makes the usual route less safe, and he recommends following local people along an easier route between Longbanga Tso (1st Lake) and Taujung Tso (2nd Lake). See Tenzing’s sketch of the route:.

Alternative route between Gokyo Lakes, suggested by Gokyo Tenzing Sherpa.

Tenzing also noted that the route from Thame to Gokyo is open, as the Gokyo Lodge Association cleared and reopened the trail from the Gokyo side yesterday. However, conditions on the glacier may change rapidly.

The route across Gokyo is one of the most popular side trips in the Khumbu, for those wanting to enrich their Everest Base Camp trek. The area features stunning scenery, with high mountain lakes, glaciers, and a view of the formidable South Face of Cho Oyu.

Animal Attack Roundup, Nov. 4

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (934 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Explorersweb

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, while they predominate the media reports, most animal attack victims are not tourists unwisely attempting to take selfies with wildlife.
  • As expanding populations push human settlements further into wildlife habitat, we can expect to see more conflicts.
  • Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Tisha Mukherjee, CC BY-SA 4.0.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, while they predominate the media reports, most animal attack victims are not tourists unwisely attempting to take selfies with wildlife. People who live and work every day among animals are the ones who most often face the consequences.

As expanding populations push human settlements further into wildlife habitat, we can expect to see more conflicts. Here are some recent incidents.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Tisha Mukherjee, CC BY-SA 4.0.

In Indonesia, 24-year-old Selviana Ambu Kaka was attacked by a crocodile while washing clothes in the Bondo Kodi River. Her fiancé and his sister witnessed a large crocodile emerging from the water, biting Ambu Kaka on the leg, and dragging her into the river. They immediately alerted nearby relatives and authorities, and a search commenced.

It has been revealed that the people of Southwest Sumba, the closest town, organized and combed the area with nets. When they found a large crocodile matching witness descriptions, they hauled it onto shore and killed it. The animal measured nearly 4.9 meters long.

Sources indicate that early on the morning of October 24, Ambu Kaka’s remains were found approximately 30m from the attack site. She is one of many such victims in Indonesia, which sees more saltwater crocodile attacks than any other country.

It has been revealed that habitat destruction is largely behind the massive number of human-crocodile conflicts. It’s an understandably hard sell, however, for conservation workers to convince locals that preventing attacks means protecting the perpetrators.

The victim had recently returned from Jakarta to become formally engaged on October 30.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons/ Rohit Gangwal, CC BY-SA 4.0.

A 65-year-old farm laborer, Tulsi Rama Sawar, was killed by a leopard in state of Maharashtra, just north of Mumbai, on November 1. The noise of the attack summoned help from the locals. By the time they arrived, the leopard had fled, but Sawar was deceased. Her case comes less than a month after a leopard killed a 52-year-old woman in the same area.

Town residents are demanding immediate government action to capture the animal. If their demands for cage traps and cameras are not granted, locals threaten collective protest. The attacks represent a threat to their lives, but also their livelihoods, as farmers are unable to work the fields out of fear of attack.

Elsewhere, in Uttar Pradesh near the Nepal border, a 45-year-old farmer named Kennu fought off an attacking leopard, sustaining serious injuries. The man was working in a sugarcane field when the predator leaped out from hiding. Kennu fought back, and the animal retreated long enough for him to flee home, where family members brought him to medical care. Forestry officials have urged agricultural workers to avoid working in the fields alone.

Recent findings suggest that farm workers are not the only leopard victims, however. Early in the morning of November 4, a 15-year-old girl was dragged from her home in the Shahdol district of central India.

Saraswati Singh Gond was sleeping in bed beside her sister on their veranda, which did not have a door. A leopard entered during the night, not even waking her sister. Singh Gond’s body was found approximately 300m from the house. The search for the leopard continues.

Photo: Wikimedia Commons/Shadow Ayush, CC BY-SA 4.0.

Leopards are only one of the wildlife threats that rural Indians face. A 55-year-old woman was gathering mushrooms in Utterakand in northern India on October 30 when she was attacked and killed by a wild elephant. Devaki Rana was lifted up and thrown to the ground, her son reported.

The incident occurred in one of India’s elephant corridors, which allow highly endangered Asian elephant herds to move between their fragmented habitats. The corridors are essential to conservation, but also present a concentrated area where attacks are more common.

Industry observers note that another fatal encounter took place in the state of Chhattisgarh in east-central India. A man of between 35 and 40 years of age, traveling by motorcycle with his nephew, came upon an elephant standing in the road. It immediately charged them, killing the uncle, while his nephew managed to hide beneath a parked truck. Eventually, the elephant left, and he was able to escape.

Locals believe that the elephant in question is one known as Kabra Kaan, which they see frequently and which has been connected with earlier incidents. The Forestry Department, however, has not confirmed this.

According to recent reports, elephant corridors allow them to pass between the remaining forested areas. Photo: Wildlife Trust of India.

It has been revealed that in Japan, brown bear attacks have been rising for several years. As in many places, human settlements are encroaching on brown bear territory. A decrease in farmland has left no boundary between the urban and the forested worlds. The government has responded with controversial bear culls, despite the concerns of conservation workers.

The latest incident is very different from the increasingly common attack stories. Late on the night of October 30, an express train running on Hokkaido’s Soya Line collided with a large brown bear. The body of the bear was trapped under the train, and the wheels derailed.

Industry observers note that A brown bear became trapped beneath the wheels of Sarobetsu No 3. Photo: Hokkaido Railway Firm.

According to recent reports, none of the crew or 32 passengers were injured in the crash. However, fearing more bears were in the area, officials kept everyone on the train overnight, until they could be safely extracted the following morning. Manufacturer officials have confirmed that this is the first bear-collision derailment in their nearly 40-year history.
